origin: constructed English practice contrasts; not external corpus or perceptual gold

cases.expectation: Both careful would-you and natural /dʒ/ blending are permitted. The deliberately voiceless /tʃ/ is the contrast to identify.
Both careful don't-you and natural /tʃ/ blending are permitted. The deliberately voiced /dʒ/ is the contrast to identify.

cases.text: Ten bags are in the car.
cases.expectation: Unassimilated /n/ and bilabial /m/ before bags are permitted; the velar /ŋ/ is an inappropriate place change in this context.
This is an explicit smooth-linking practice contrast. Careful non-linked speech is permitted outside that task; an intrusive boundary is not a universal accent error.
Neutral weak-form practice contrasts weak to with a full stressed to. Strong to is permitted in a genuinely contrastive context.

cases.text: We need the documents, not one document.
cases.expectation: The audible context requires plural documents. A permitted /t/ elision retains /s/; the target removes the complete plural-bearing ending.

cases.text: I can pay for the car.
cases.expectation: Only the selected weak for-the interval is stretched to 1.5x. Remaining speech samples/timing and lexical stress stay preserved.
A 600 ms intrusive pause occurs between the article and noun, not at an acceptable clause boundary.
In this explicit statement practice, the reference falls and the contrast rises. The words are identical to the confirmation-question item.
In this explicit confirmation-question practice, the reference rises and the contrast falls. The lexical words match the statement item.
A normal information-seeking WH-question is permitted to fall despite its question mark. The rising version is a context-specific contour contrast, not universally wrong.

cases.text: I am not sure yet. Maybe.
cases.expectation: The audible uncertainty setup supports the requested fall-rise practice contrast. The exercise compares that contour with a decisive fall.
The audible certainty setup supports an emphatic rise-fall contrast against a continuing rise.
